# task-5fae7846: horizontal object settling

## Rule confirmed by demo and test
Treat each orthogonally connected same-color nonzero component as a rigid object. Move all objects rightward, preserving their shape and color, until blocked by the right grid edge or another object. Objects can move simultaneously but cannot overlap. The demo confirms the input arrangement settles exactly to the right: each colored component reaches a final position with no cell able to advance further. Color 8 cells participate as objects as well; isolated 8 markers slide independently unless blocked.

## Important component grouping and motion
- Same-color orthogonally adjacent cells belong together as one rigid component. Diagonal touching does not connect components.
- Motion is horizontal only (no gravity/vertical movement).
- The operation is repeated rightward settling, not a uniform translation of the entire grid and not a shift where gaps persist unnecessarily.
- Treat collision against other colored objects as a blocker. The update can be simulated by repeatedly advancing any component one cell right if all its cells have empty or self-occupied destinations, until no component can advance. This simultaneous/iterative formulation handles a front object clearing space for trailing objects and avoids any ambiguity in ordering.
- Zeros are empty background; preserve dimensions.

# task-5fae7846: horizontal object settling

## Rule confirmed by demo and test
Treat each orthogonally connected same-color nonzero component as a rigid object. Move all objects rightward, preserving shape and color, until blocked by the right grid edge or another object. Objects can move simultaneously but cannot overlap. The demo confirms the input arrangement settles exactly to the right: each colored component reaches a final position with no cell able to advance further. Color 8 cells participate as objects as well; isolated 8 markers slide independently unless blocked.

## Important component grouping and motion
- Same-color orthogonally adjacent cells belong together as one rigid component. Diagonal touching does not connect components.
- Motion is horizontal only (no gravity/vertical movement).
- The operation is repeated rightward settling, not a uniform translation of the entire grid and not a shift where gaps persist unnecessarily.
- Treat collision against other colored objects as a blocker. The update can be simulated by repeatedly advancing any component one cell right if all its cells have empty or self-occupied destinations, until no component can advance. This simultaneous/iterative formulation handles a front object clearing space for trailing objects and avoids any ambiguity in ordering.
- Zeros are empty background; preserve dimensions.

## Verified test instance
Input 10x10 components included 8 at (0,3),(5,3),(7,1),(9,5); 2 shape [(0,5),(1,5),(1,6)]; 2 vertical pair [(2,0),(3,0)]; 3 at row 2 columns 2-4; 4 shape [(3,4),(3,6),(4,4-6)]; 6 vertical at rows 6-7 col6; 5 pair at row8 cols3-4. Every component moved right until blocked/edge. Correct output:

 [0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0,8],

 [0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0,5,5],
 [0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0,8]]

## Failed attempt / lesson

The corrected output stopped the 2 component at columns 8-9 on lower row and column 8 on top row, while 8 remains at top row column 7."
